transcript: if you're not familiar with his game you should know that Oscar winner Tarell Alvin McCraney fully made me cry and even if you can't make it to see this play before it closes in a couple weeks at least do yourself a favor and check out his other work this is a revival of his 2007 play The Brothers Size and it blends traditional Yoruba storytelling elements with a modern fable about brotherhood and life after incarceration aside from offering a lot of emotional insight into that experience it's also just a beautiful piece of drama with characters that you really like and really root for and even relate to in a certain sense like I haven't experienced most of what these characters have experienced but I do have a brother and even on that level it resonated with me very deeply to the point where I was kind of an emotional wreck in the second half and something special about this specific revival is that not only is Tarell Alvin Mccraney co-directing this production but it also stars Andre Holland who was in Moonlight the movie that Tarell Alvin Mccraney won an Oscar for co writing Mccraney’s work also hasn't had a (major?) New York production in almost seven years I think the last one was when Choir Boy was on Broadway and that was one of the best plays I've ever seen for my money he's really one of the great playwrights of his generation but New York audiences haven't had many opportunities to see his work recently so if you haven't seen any of his plays on stage before I really would not recommend missing this one but you better get on it because it closes on September 28th at the Shed
